WDF1-Portfolio-Custom-Domain/README.md.content: # Portfolio: modules, forms and a static build This lab continues the HTML, CSS and DOM portfolio with a separate JavaScript validation module and a local project-idea form. WDF0-WDF2 use the original [four-file edition](basics/README.md). This module edition is a new saved project: retain the earlier files and transfer intended content edits into it. ## Files and roles Each role has `index.html`, `styles.css`, `main.js`, `project-idea.js` and `package.json`. HTML supplies landmarks, project cards, labels and native form constraints. CSS controls layout and focus. `main.js` handles DOM events and safe rendering; it imports `validateProjectIdea` from `project-idea.js`. The validator reads values and returns a result without accessing the DOM. The starter keeps that validator as a deliberate TODO and refuses previews until it is implemented. The reference implements the same stated contract. Both keep the original deployment list and year behavior. Compare the reference after completing and checking the starter. ## Run from the complete repository Use Node.js 24. From the repository root with its maintained package and lockfiles, select exactly one role: ```sh npm ci --workspace WDF1-Portfolio-Custom-Domain/starter npm run dev --workspace WDF1-Portfolio-Custom-Domain/starter -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port 5173 --strictPort ``` Open `http://127.0.0.1:5173`. Stop this process with Ctrl+C. Replace `starter` with `solution` in those commands to inspect the reference separately, with the first role stopped. A role-only ZIP omits the root monorepo lockfile; place its edited files back into the selected complete-repository workspace before using these commands. Do not replace that root lockfile with a new one. ```sh node --test test/portfolio-project-idea.test.mjs npm run build --workspace WDF1-Portfolio-Custom-Domain/starter npm run preview --workspace WDF1-Portfolio-Custom-Domain/starter -- --host 127.0.0.1 --port 4173 --strictPort ``` The default Node tests check the reference. Run the same contract against the learner's starter with: ```sh node test/portfolio-project-idea.test.mjs starter ``` The unfinished starter initially fails the valid-input cases. Complete its validator and repeat until all five cases pass. Preview serves `dist` at `http://127.0.0.1:4173`; stop it with Ctrl+C after the browser checks. ## Validation contract `validateProjectIdea(fields)` returns either `{ ok: true, value: { projectTitle, projectType, goal } }` or `{ ok: false, errors: { fieldName: "Useful message" } }`. - Accept only string fields. Trim surrounding whitespace from title and goal. - A trimmed title has length 1-60; a trimmed goal has length 1-200. Length uses JavaScript string length, the same units as the HTML maxlength controls. - Type is exactly `website`, `game` or `data`; an unexpected value is refused. - Validation reports errors without mutating its input or touching the page. - Valid text is displayed using `textContent`, never interpreted as markup. - Empty controls receive native browser feedback. A whitespace-only value needs the JavaScript check. An invalid result clears an earlier preview, announces the errors and focuses its first invalid control. - A valid submit replaces the previous preview. Clear resets both controls and preview. Refresh discards the draft; this project sends no form request. Try all three types, whitespace-only text, exact limits and values one unit beyond the limits by calling the validator. In the form, try keyboard-only submit and reset, repeated submit, a long unbroken word, a Unicode title and literal `text` as a goal. The last value must appear literally. ## Explain the boundaries An `export` names a module binding; `import` names the binding used by another module. The page's `type="module"` entry allows that dependency graph. During development Vite serves source modules; a build transforms their dependency graph and writes static output. The module must not be omitted from an export. Native `required` and `maxlength` constraints help the person using the form. They do not establish a future API's trust boundary. A later server must validate again before storage or delivery. The current form only previews fictional data in the browser. This lab requires no environment file. In Vite, `VITE_` values are public client configuration substituted into a build. A database password or SMTP credential belongs on a server and must never be put in browser source or a client build variable. Ignoring a file in Git does not remove it from a build that explicitly reads and publishes its contents. ## Browser and build check At 390 and 1280 CSS pixels, and separately at 200% zoom, check source heading order, field labels, keyboard operation, visible focus, long-text wrapping, status feedback and the absence of horizontal scrolling. Make one original project section and explain its semantic heading. Inspect Console and Network before and after a successful build. The locally previewed build must show the same intended content and form behavior. Public hosting and custom-domain configuration are later work, not requirements for this local lab. References: [JavaScript modules](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Guide/Modules), [form validation](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Learn_web_development/Extensions/Forms/Form_validation), [Vite environment values](https://vite.dev/guide/env-and-mode).
